We know one student got 95% on the exam.  
The other student got 3 wrong out of 40, so that student got \(40 - 3 = 37\) correct.  
To find that student’s percentage:  
\[
\frac{37}{40} = 0.925 = 92.5\%
\]  
So the highest score so far is 95%.  
To beat 95%, Sierra needs more than 95% of 40 questions:  
\[
0.95 \times 40 = 38
\]  
So 38 correct gives exactly 95%, which ties but does not beat.  
She needs at least 39 correct to have a higher percentage.  

Final answer: 39
